description:
FILED s418 (Fable), found by the B2 (#343) acceptance probes on the
split.t:503 shape.  PRE-EXISTING and independent of the ceiling fix (a plain
one-liner shows it; no list-operator parse involved).

    perl -e q(print chr(160) =~ /\s/u ? "match" : "no")     perl: match
    the same through PCL                                     PCL:  no

perl: under /u (Unicode rules), \s matches every White_Space character,
including U+00A0 NBSP (and \x{85} NEL); since 5.18, \s and [[:space:]] agree.
PCL answers "no" for NBSP, so its \s under /u is the ASCII set.

Consequence measured in the sweep population: perl-tests/split.t:503
(my ($sp) = grep /\s/u, map chr, reverse 128 .. 255 or skip ...) finds \xA0
under perl and takes the skip branch under PCL.  That skip is the file
authors own guard for engines without high-bit whitespace, so the behavior
is graceful â but any test asserting the /u semantics directly will diverge.

Fix belongs in the regex lowering/runtime where \s is translated (find the
sibling: how does \w under /u fare? \d?).  Check what the CL regex engine
offers for property classes before hand-rolling a set.
title: \s under /u does not match NBSP (U+00A0) â ASCII-only \s in Unicode mode
